record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Which words w can be obtained in more than one way from a single word u using different conducting sequences?

evidence.quote: Which words w can be obtained in more than one way from a single word u using different conducting sequences?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ denote the set of finite words over $A$. For a word $u=u_1u_2\cdots u_n\in A^*$ of length $n$, a *conducting sequence* is a word $c=c_1c_2\cdots c_{2n}\in\{1,2\}^{2n}$ in which the symbol $1$ occurs exactly $n$ times and the symbol $2$ occurs exactly $n$ times. Given $u$ and a conducting sequence $c$, define the *shuffle of $u$ with itself directed by $c$* to be the word $w=w_1w_2\cdots w_{2n}\in A^{2n}$ obtained as follows: scan $c$ from left to right; the $k$-th occurrence of the symbol $1$ in $c$ contributes $u_k$ to $w$ at that position, and the $k$-th occurrence of the symbol $2$ in $c$ also contributes $u_k$ to $w$ at that position. Equivalently, $w$ is an interleaving of two copies of $u$ in which $c$ records which copy each letter of $w$ comes from.

Characterize all words $w\in A^{2n}$ for which there exists a single word $u\in A^n$ and two distinct conducting sequences $c\neq c'$ in $\{1,2\}^{2n}$ such that the shuffle of $u$ with itself directed by $c$ and the shuffle of $u$ with itself directed by $c'$ both equal $w$. That is, describe precisely those words $w$ that can be obtained as a self-shuffle of some single word $u$ in more than one way via different conducting sequences.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published characterization addressing exactly this question of which words admit more than one conducting sequence as a self-shuffle of a single word $u$. Related work on shuffle squares and shuffled-square-free words (e.g., Müller on shuffling infinite square-free words; Harju; Buss–Soltys on NP-completeness of shuffle-square recognition; and later work by Guégan–Ochem and Juge) studies existence and decision problems but does not appear to settle this characterization, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: On shuffling of infinite square-free words (Müller)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies shuffles of square-free words and conducting sequences, but does not give a characterization of words obtainable in multiple ways from a single word.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related literature on square-free shuffles does not contain the requested characterization.

status_evidence.title: On shuffled-square-free words (Juge)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves bounds on alphabet size for infinite shuffled-square-free words; focuses on existence rather than uniqueness of conducting sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress addresses different aspects of shuffle-squares than the multiplicity of conducting sequences.
